text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 23,440.8, up 1.68% on the day and 3.02% over the past five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.58% (5‑day +2.93%). Advances outpaced declines sharply – 401 stocks rose versus 92 fell – giving a breadth score of 44.5 in a neutral zone. The move was fairly broad, with 41% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average and 35.8% above the 200‑day average, indicating momentum across many sectors.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 3,114.68 cr today, extending a four‑day buying streak, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 392.2 cr, marking a second consecutive day of net outflow. Leading sectors were Pharma, Infrastructure, Oil & Gas, Healthcare, PSU banks and Commodities; weakening areas included IT, Media and Private banks. Options data show a put‑call ratio of 1.66 for Nifty (more puts than calls) and a max‑pain level near 23,250, with a call wall at 24,000 and a put wall at 23,000, suggesting resistance around those points.

Watch the Nifty 50 pivot levels – support at 23,284.97 (S1) and pivot at 23,362.88 – for the next session. A break below the 23,284 support could test the 20‑day EMA around 23,200, while a hold above the 24,000 call wall may allow the index to target the upper range of 23,588‑23,888. Keep an eye on global cues such as Brent crude falling 9.5% and US equity futures modestly higher, which could influence risk appetite.
